excerpts.text:
During the remainder of this century, some countries will see population growth and some will see population decline. For example, the UN projects that [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria") will gain about 340 million people, about the present population of the US, to become the third most populous country, and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") will lose about half of its population.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:10-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:11-7)

Even though the global fertility rate continues to fall, chart #2 shows that because of [population momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_momentum "Population momentum") the global population will continue to grow, although at a steadily slower rate, until the mid-2080s (the median line).

It expected that a slowing of the population growth rate will lead to a population peak of 10.4 billion in 2086 in the medium scenario, after which it would then begin to slowly fall. This shift from earlier projections of peak population and predicted date of zero population growth comes from a more rapid drop in Africa's birth rate than previous projections had expected.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:2-23) For example, the 2012 report predicted that the population of Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, would rise to 914 million by 2100; the 2022 report lowers that to 546 million, a reduction of 368 million; the 2024 report lowered that further to 477 million, a reduction of 69 million.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:1-18)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:11-7)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:2-23) Jose Rimon of Johns Hopkins University suggested, "We have been underestimating what is happening in terms of fertility change in Africa. Africa will probably undergo the same kind of rapid changes as east Asia did."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-:2-23) The 2024 edition brought the peak forward to 2084, with the population topping at 10.3 billion.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_population_projections#cite_note-24)
